body.title: migration(forgejo): migrate reactions and reviews
body.body:
- Forgejo advertises pre-release version (eg [`17.0.0-26-363f3dc30b+gitea-1.22.0`](https://code.forgejo.org/api/v1/version)). 
- Such pre-releases version never fullfix the `hashicorp/go-version.Constraints.Check` used by `gitea_sdk.Client.CheckServerVersionConstraint`.

Hence migration from a Forgejo host (like codeberg) would wrongly skip reactions and reviews (and use a weaker pagination)

This fixes this, by using `Version.GreaterThanOrEqual` instead.

body.title: perf: do not terminate CatFileBatch[Check] subprocess on git.ErrNotExist errors
body.body:
In #13756, new interfaces were added to access the reusable git subprocesses `git cat-file --batch` and `git cat-file --batch-check`.  One change involved in that was that errors returned from methods using those subprocesses were considered to leave the subprocesses in an unusable state -- the subprocess would be closed on any error.  While reviewing the performance of #15148, I noted that `git.ErrNotExist` is often returned from these subprocesses when checking for commits, tags, and other references that don't exist.  These errors do not leave the subprocess streams in an invalid state, but rather indicate successful identification of a missing object in the git repo.

This PR omits `git.ErrNotExist` from the errors that close the subprocesses, allowing them to be reused after checking that a commit doesn't exist.

body.title: feat: preserve force-push commits on PRs through `git gc`
body.body:
Implements #8279.

Whenever a force push occurs on an open PR (via branch or AGit), an additional reference is created in the base git in the form of `refs/pull/N/comment/M/{old,new}`.  `N` is the pull request index, `M` is the internal ID of the timeline comment on the PR, and `old` or `new` are used for either the commit previous to the force push, or the commit after the force push.  The new references are read-only and cannot be modified or deleted by external `git push` operations.  The references are removed if the pull request is deleted (but not if the pull request is closed).

### Excessive memory allocation when decompressing crafted streams in github.com/andybalholm/brotli
BIT-brotli-2026-111497 / BIT-dotnet-2026-111497 / BIT-dotnet-sdk-2026-111497 / BIT-node-2026-111497 / BIT-node-min-2026-111497 / BIT-powershell-2026-111497 / [CVE-2026-111497](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-111497) / [GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35) / [GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv) / [GO-2026-6888](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6888) / PYSEC-2026-4322 / PYSEC-2026-4323

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
In github.com/andybalholm/brotli before v1.2.7, the decompressor allocates memory for Huffman tables and block-type trees on every meta-block header without bounding the cumulative allocations relative to the input size. A small crafted brotli stream containing many empty meta-blocks with new Huffman trees can trigger hundreds of megabytes of allocations per kilobyte of input, leading to denial of service.

#### Severity
Unknown

#### References
